Theme

Latin word

ipsī

ipsī, ipsae, ipsa

pronoun, intensive (plural of ipse), declension

ourselves (for emphasis: we ourselves); themselves (for emphasis: they themselves, of their own accord); yourselves (for emphasis: you yourselves)

In this lexicon

  • ourselves

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.14: sī nōsmet ipsōs regere possumus (Lewis & Short, s.v. agō)

  • themselves

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. NH 18.107: ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs; Cic. Div. 1.74: valvae clausae sē ipsae aperuērunt (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse, Div. 1.37.74)

  • yourselves

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 104: ut ea contrā vōsmet ipsōs facere videāminī (Lewis & Short, s.v. contrā)

Examples

  • ut nōsmet ipsī inter nōs conjūnctiōrēs sīmus

    so that we ourselves may be closer to each otherCic. Att. 14.13B.5 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for ourselves

  • pistōrēs Rōmae nōn fuēre ad Persicum ūsque bellum … ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs, mulierumque id opus maximē erat

    There were no bakers at Rome until the war with Perseus … the citizens made their bread themselves, and it was chiefly the women’s work.Plin. NH 18.107

    In the entry for themselves

  • jam hortum ipsī agricolae succīdiam alteram appellant

    And the garden the farmers themselves call their second flitch of bacon.Cic. Sen. 56
